findings.summary: The note mixes up the producer median and the headline median per landed job. The fix cannot visibly reverse a rise of about 687 minutes.
findings.evidence: The headline is the median of total minutes per landed job (`median_windows`, status.rs:1188), and it rose from 918.1 to 1604.8, about 687 minutes. The producer median rose only 10.8 minutes, and the listed stage medians together rose about 18. The plan's caveat ('may not lower the median by the whole 10.8 minutes') mixes up the two. Even if the fix works fully, it accounts for about 1.6% of the headline rise (an estimate from the request's figures). Fix: In the note, separate the two figures. Say the fix targets the producer median. Say most of the headline rise is not explained by the stage medians the request lists (for example, a median of totals is not a sum of medians, and the landing-and-rebuild spread matters), so the headline may not visibly fall. Add this as an open question for the user.
findings.location: Plan, Risks and Step 6 section (8); request acceptance 'the next throughput review shows the median minutes per landed job falling'

findings.summary: The cost of the removed command can be measured, but the plan leaves it as an estimate.
findings.evidence: The producer can run cargo, and its CARGO_TARGET_DIR is a cold per-job directory (athena.toml:80). So the cost of the removed command can be measured, not only estimated. The plan relies on that cost to tie the cause to the 10.8-minute rise, yet labels it an estimate without trying to measure it. Fix: Add a step: time `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` in a fresh target directory, and again after a docs-only job's usual builds (or after `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`). Report both as measured in this environment, and still label the per-job share an estimate.
findings.location: Approach ('nothing below is measured'); Risks item 1; Step 6

findings.summary: The plan treats d0ff1e9's date as the date of the previous review, but it is the date the review code landed.
findings.evidence: In HISTORY.txt, d0ff1e9 (2026-11-04) is the commit that added the throughput review code. It does not record when the previous review ran. ad7e260 (2026-11-07) changed the review again. When the previous review actually ran is only in records/, which the snapshot does not have. Fix: In the note, state the 2026-11-04 date as a lower bound inferred from the code history, not as the measured date of the previous review. Add the actual review date to the Host open questions.
findings.location: Approach ('the previous review was 2026-11-04 (d0ff1e9)'); Demonstration for criterion 1

findings.summary: Step 3 asks for a 'docs-only reading' that no existing fixture provides, and the section does not depend on the reading.

summary: I checked the plan against the code and HISTORY.txt using Read and Grep, and I accept it. Its main claims hold. Commit 69057b9 (2026-11-06) touched briefs.rs. `MIRROR_CHECK_INSTRUCTION` (briefs.rs:856) is rendered into every producer brief, with no condition, by `mirror_check_section` (briefs.rs:640, 863). The producer builds in its own per-job `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (athena.toml:80, 111). Unlike checks, that directory is not linked to a warm slot directory (`BuildLink` in env.rs is used only for checks, and slot_exec.rs does no linking), so the build starts cold. The loop already runs `mirror_drift_in` in-process (producer.rs:76, 361-365, 409). The test at briefs.rs:3243-3267 is the only reader of the old command text; no other file uses the constant. The 'Files kept by hand' text appears nowhere else except D158 at decisions.md:4360. athena-context depends only on athena-data, which confirms why the conditional variant was rejected. Criterion 4 does not trip `limits_changed_files`: it has 'only' but no 'may change', and none of the other patterns. So editing briefs.rs and run/tests.rs is not blocked by an allowed-paths check, and Athena's two scope findings are weak, because those files are the cause path. Both demonstrations use real seams: `producer_brief`, and `Athena::go` through `mirror_job`. Both fail on the old text, and the run test first checks that the section is present, so its 'does not contain' assertion cannot pass vacuously. The cause is still inferred, not measured, but the plan says so, lists the other candidates and names the records that would settle them. My remaining findings are about how the note frames its evidence: (1) the headline median (918.1 to 1604.8 min) rose about 687 minutes, and a fix worth at most about 11 producer minutes cannot visibly reverse it; (2) the producer can time the removed command, which would make the key number measured instead of an estimate; (3) d0ff1e9's date is when the review code landed, not when the previous review ran.
